newsitem.title: USA: Triton to acquire Security Systems.
newsitem.headline: Triton to acquire Security Systems.

text.p: Triton Group Ltd. said Monday it has signed a letter of intent to merge with Security Systems Holdings Inc., in a stock deal worth about 22.7 million.

Security Systems is the parent of Orange, Conn.-based Alarmguard Inc., which provides security alarm monitoring services for homes and businesses in Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Maryland.

San Diego, Calif.-based Triton said it plans to issue about 33 million common shares to Security Systems in the deal. Triton shareholders will retain the 21.5 million shares and about 500,000 warrants already outstanding.
After the new shares are issued Triton's current shareholders will own 40 percent of the combined company, while Security Systems shareholders will own 60 percent.
The deal is expected to close by Dec. 31, subject to due diligence and approval by both companies' shareholders.
Triton, which emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 1993, operates as a shell company with stakes in two property investment companies, Mission West Properties and Ridgewood Properties.
Triton's stock edged down 6.25 cents to $68.75 cents on the American Stock Exchange in late trading.
